primitives.name: Banned Claim Exclusion Zone
primitives.verbatim_quote: ﻿# No-Claim Rules ## Banned claims - No win-rate claims - No ROI claims - No
primitives.assumptions: Claims are classified into performance vs. process categories; exclusion applies when C ∈ {win-rate, ROI, edge}.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Z = 1, all performance-based claims are invalid under current backtest state.

layer2.mapping: Banned claims map to forbidden regions in GSI's posterior belief space, where likelihood ratios exceed threshold bounds.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of claim categorization against backtest truth.

primitives.name: Allowed Positioning Frame
primitives.verbatim_quote: this current backtest state ## Allowed positioning - Process rigor and decision quality framing - Transparency
primitives.assumptions: Process-oriented framing is valid when F = f(R, T), where R and T are non-negative.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F > 0, claims are considered acceptable under educational or transparency framing.

layer2.mapping: Allowed positioning defines a kernel in GSE's state transition space, where decision quality drives policy evolution.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking of framing consistency in communication channels.

primitives.name: Disclaimer Inclusion Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: "No performance guarantee" - "Backtest truth currently does not show model edge over naive baseline" -
primitives.assumptions: All communications must satisfy D ⊃ {No performance guarantee, Backtest truth, No profit promise}.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If ¬(D ⊇ required_disclaimers), then communication is flagged for review.

layer2.mapping: Disclaimers act as probabilistic constraints in GSI’s epistemic confidence layer, bounding model overconfidence.
layer2.telemetry: Automated check of disclaimer completeness in all outbound messages.

This mirrors Bayesian inference where prior beliefs are constrained by evidence. The exclusion zone enforces a likelihood boundary such that any claim exceeding it is invalid. The allowed frame operates through a kernel function that maps decision quality and transparency into a valid claim space. Disclaimers function as probabilistic constraints, ensuring that model confidence does not exceed empirical support. Failure modes arise when claims slip into excluded zones or when disclaimers are omitted, leading to epistemic overreach. These primitives form a closed-loop system where GSI's posterior belief updates are bounded by GSE's decision transitions, maintaining alignment between inference and action.
